title: Different paths are possible
caption: Illustrative developmental trajectories, not observed study data. The same starting point can be followed by improvement, fluctuation, or later difficulty. A trajectory describes a pattern; it does not determine an individual future.

title: From a claim to a proportionate conclusion
caption: A research claim becomes more trustworthy when the question, measurement, design, ethics, and alternative explanations are made explicit. The final conclusion must remain within the limits of the evidence.

title: Two different questions about change
caption: Between-person differences and within-person fluctuations are distinct sources of variation. A longitudinal analysis should state which question its parameters answer. This schematic contains no empirical estimates.
nodes: Who generally has more support or distress?
Is this child different from their own usual pattern?
Do schools and families change the pattern?

title: One concern, several theoretical lenses
caption: Theories direct attention to different mechanisms. An integrated formulation explains why particular lenses are useful for this child and setting, rather than treating every explanation as equally supported.

title: Developmental tasks and changing contexts
caption: Age bands are approximate and overlap. Communication, culture, health, and responsibility affect how a child experiences each transition. The diagram is a guide to questions, not a checklist of universal milestones.

title: Development is a transaction over time
caption: A child’s characteristics and participation influence the environment, and the environment influences later learning and adaptation. Biological and social processes are connected rather than competing explanations.
nodes: What the child does and seeks

title: Capacity is used under conditions
caption: A young person’s ability to use a skill depends on more than whether the skill exists. Emotion, peer pressure, fatigue, familiarity, and support can affect performance in the moment. This is a conceptual map, not an anatomical brain model.

title: The learning sequence has feedback
caption: Setting events influence how an immediate antecedent is experienced. The consequence can change the likelihood of the behavior on a later occasion. The child’s account helps distinguish escape, access, communication, and other possible functions.

title: Performance depends on the whole task
caption: Understanding, language access, working memory, emotional safety, and organization all contribute to observed performance. Assess where the task breaks down before attributing the difficulty to motivation or general ability.
nodes: Can steps be held and ordered?

title: A score is one part of a decision
caption: Responsible assessment begins with a referral question and checks the fit, quality, and uncertainty of measurement. Test results meet developmental and functional evidence before a decision is made, and the decision is reviewed.

title: An account has a communication history
caption: Experience, attention, later information, retrieval conditions, and questioning can influence what is reported. Protect neutral communication and distinguish therapeutic support from investigative evidence gathering.

title: Emotion and response form a cycle
caption: Appraisal, arousal, action, and other people’s responses influence one another. Co-regulation and environmental change can alter the cycle. The diagram does not imply that every emotion follows the same sequence.
nodes: What seems to be at stake?

title: Self-understanding develops in context
caption: The self is shaped through action, relationships, group membership, and social recognition. A formulation should include contexts of confidence as well as experiences that impose narrow conditions of worth.
nodes: What I can do and learn

title: Peer experience shapes the next expectation
caption: Interpretation and peer responses can form a feedback loop. Real exclusion must be addressed directly; changing a child’s interpretation is not a substitute for changing an unsafe environment.

title: Helping requires a safe route to action
caption: Witnessing harm does not automatically lead to helping. Safety, responsibility, practical skills, group norms, and reliable adult responses influence whether a child can act. Support afterward is also a form of help.

title: Resilience is supported by systems
caption: Positive adaptation depends on interacting resources and conditions over time. A child’s skills matter, but relationships, institutional access, and material safety also shape what is possible.

title: Similar concerns can have different pathways
caption: Equifinality means that different processes can lead to a similar presenting concern. Multifinality means that a shared starting condition can lead to different outcomes. The arrows are hypotheses to investigate, not predictions for a particular child.

title: Support improves the person–environment fit
caption: Participation can improve through teaching skills, changing demands, and providing accessible supports. A diagnosis informs this process but does not prescribe one identical plan for every child.

title: Intervention is a learning cycle
caption: A formulation guides a proportionate plan. Practice and monitoring reveal whether the proposed mechanism is relevant and whether the intervention can be used in daily life. New information may require revision of the original formulation.

title: Doctoral integration keeps the child in view
caption: Evidence, developmental theory, lived experience, ethics, and outcome monitoring inform one another. Professional judgment remains accountable to the child’s welfare and to new information.
